window: Games played Sept. 3–7, 2026 (Week 0 and unplayed Week 2 excluded)
source_engines: Three-engine compilation (Claude Opus 5, Gemini 3.8, GPT Astra 6), cross-checked Sept. 9. The engines picked three different winners (Toney / Chambliss / Heintschel); the merged verdict applies the published criteria — opponent quality and game-deciding execution broke the tie toward Chambliss, whose win over No. 24 Louisville was the week's only ranked-vs-ranked game and ended in a walk-off two-minute drill. Fact conflicts resolved: Chambliss 60 rush yds (2-of-3 engines; one said 50), Toney's long TD 47 (2-of-3; one said 48), Moore 378 yds (box score of record, resolving an early 388 wire figure).

athlete_of_the_week.stat_line: 21/36, 336 pass yds, 3 pass TD, 1 INT; 9 car, 60 rush yds, 1 rush TD — 396 total yds, 4 total TD
athlete_of_the_week.result: W 41-38 vs. No. 24 Louisville (Music City Kickoff, Nashville, Sept. 6, 2026)
athlete_of_the_week.why: The only Week 1 game matching two AP Top 25 programs, and Chambliss decided it: four total touchdowns — including two 62-yard third-quarter strikes and a fourth-quarter TD pass plus a keeper — after a turnover-marred first half, then an eight-play, 44-yard two-minute drill in the final 88 seconds, capped by an 18-yard third-and-6 completion under blitz that set up the walk-off 48-yard field goal. Highest opponent-quality score on the board with the week's defining execution.

runners_up.stat_line: 12 rec (13 targets), 234 rec yds, 3 TD (long 47), 19.5 yds/rec
runners_up.why: Broke Miami's 42-year-old single-game receiving record (Eddie Brown's 220 from the 1984 Hail Flutie game), personally out-gained Stanford's entire passing offense, and scored three of six Hurricane touchdowns against a Power 4 opponent that entered 1-0. One engine's pick for the week; landed second on the merged board only because the game was never in doubt.

runners_up.stat_line: 31/41, 453 pass yds, 7 pass TD, 0 INT — TDs to seven different receivers; 476 total yds
runners_up.why: Tied the ACC single-game touchdown record with seven scores to seven different receivers and no interceptions — the first 450-yard/7-TD/0-INT game in the FBS since Joe Burrow in 2019 — earning Maxwell and Davey O'Brien national weekly honors. The statistical ceiling of Week 1; the MAC opponent discount is the only thing between him and the top spot.

runners_up.stat_line: 27/30 (90.0%), 401 pass yds, 5 pass TD, 0 INT — 257.3 rating; 406 total yds
runners_up.why: Set Miami debut records for passing yards and touchdowns while completing 90% of his throws in roughly two and a half quarters. Only the misfortune of sharing a box score with Toney's record night keeps him off the top line.

runners_up.stat_line: 16/28, 230 pass yds, 1 pass TD, 1 INT; 12 car, 113 rush yds, 2 rush TD — 343 total yds, 3 total TD
runners_up.why: The best opponent any Week 1 headliner faced, and the most complete dual-threat line: 113 rushing yards and two second-quarter scores that built a 31-3 halftime lead in Lane Kiffin's debut, anchoring 644 yards of offense in the most lopsided result between preseason-relevant programs. Named SEC Offensive Player of the Week.

honorable_mentions.stat_line: 28/37, 378 pass yds (career high), 3 pass TD, 0 INT
honorable_mentions.why: Career-high yardage and the 62-yard fourth-quarter strike to Dakorien Moore that saved No. 2 Oregon from the week's biggest upset.

honorable_mentions.stat_line: 26/36, 430 pass yds (career high), 3 pass TD, 2 INT; 463 total yds
honorable_mentions.result: W 27-24 at Florida State (Labor Day Monday)
honorable_mentions.why: Overcame a near-two-hour stadium power delay to win at Doak Campbell, capping a nine-play, 71-yard drive with a 20-yard field goal with 21 seconds left.

honorable_mentions.stat_line: 35 car, 227 rush yds, 2 rush TD; 3 rec, 19 yds — 246 scrimmage yds
honorable_mentions.why: The national Week 1 rushing high — 227 yards on 35 carries against the reigning AAC champion, with clock-killing marches of 10 and 7 minutes. Doak Walker National RB of the Week.

honorable_mentions.stat_line: 6 rec (9 targets), 126 rec yds, 1 TD — the 47-yard Hail Mary as time expired
honorable_mentions.why: Caught the restored-second Hail Mary that flipped a loss into a win — the week's single most decisive play — while accounting for roughly three-quarters of Michigan's receiving yards.

honorable_mentions.stat_line: 19 car, 183 rush yds, 4 rush TD (9.6 ypc, long 74); 1 rec, 18 yds
honorable_mentions.why: Four rushing touchdowns at 9.6 yards a carry, including the 74-yarder that broke the game open — also receiving On3 Heisman Poll votes.

criteria_note: Merged weights across the three engines: statistical dominance versus a legitimate opponent (45–60%), a single defining play or performance that decided a consequential game (30–35%), and team success that week (10–20%). FCS and MAC opponents were discounted under criterion 1, which capped Heintschel and removed Tennessee's five-touchdown freshman (Faizon Brandon vs. Furman) and Jeremiah Smith's half of work vs. Ball State from the top five. Jordan Ross (LSU EDGE — 4 tackles, a sack, and a 30-yard pick-six vs. Clemson, 94.0 PFF grade) was the last cut.
